about: The egress channel frame codec, as test vectors (egress plan E7). src/egress/frame.ts and the in-image mux (E9, images/worker/mux.mjs) are both held to this file: test/egress-frame.test.ts and test/egress-mux.test.ts.
Hex is lower-case; spaces in it are for reading and carry nothing. A wire is LENGTH(4) TYPE(1) FLOW(4) PAYLOAD, integers unsigned big-endian; LENGTH counts the payload only.
frames: each one must encode to its wire, byte for byte.

scripts: run in order on one channel of the role named (a kernel channel holds the limits given; a mux channel learns them from go). send: the frame must be sent, as wire. refuse: the send must be refused with that refusal, and change nothing. receive: the pieces, fed in order, must decode to exactly those frames and then the refusal, if one is named; the pieces may be split or joined at any byte without changing that. finish: the other end's stream has ended; the refusal, if one is named, must be returned. openFlows and flowsOpened, on any step, must hold after it.

Each end's scripts meet every refusal that end can meet, receiving (and at finish) and sending, so a mux codec that replays only the mux scripts (E9) is held to every refusal a mux can meet. Between them the two ends' scripts meet every refusal in FRAME_REFUSALS, which lists them in the check order src/egress/frame.ts documents.

Each end's scripts also refuse a payload of every wrong length that end can meet, each way: each type under its least and past a fixed most (length), and a data, stdout or stderr past frameMaxBytes (oversize). test/egress-frame.test.ts lists them as LENGTH_CELLS.

A frame that breaks more than one rule is refused by the first it breaks in that check order; src/egress/frame.ts says, rule by rule, when a frame breaks each. A script named 'check order, X before Y' (or 'X before Y and Z') ends with one frame, received or sent, that breaks exactly the rules it names, and must be refused with X, the first of them. Wherever one frame can break two rules, the first it breaks and another, at an end and a way (receiving or sending) that can meet it, a check-order script of that end and way names both: test/egress-frame.test.ts finds every such place with a second evaluator of those rules over the states an end can reach, lists them as ORDER_PAIRS, and holds these names and frames to them.
